conservation.help_by: Respect distance on the reef; support healthy fish stocks sharks need.
conservation.caution_against: Don’t bait, chase, or grab rays and sharks for photos.

life_info.eating: Clams, snails, and crabs crushed with plate-like teeth. Digs in sand with a duck-like snout, then crunches lunch.
life_info.mating: Live-bearing; pups arrive ready to swim.
life_info.habitat: Sandy flats and reef passes; sometimes leaps clear of the water. May cruise alone or in elegant small squadrons.

fun_facts: Polka dots on a flying carpet — one of the ocean’s best costumes.
Those leaps might shake off remoras… or just show off.

conservation.help_by: Give wildlife space; pick reef-safe sunscreen and careful finning.
conservation.caution_against: Don’t feed fish, chase animals, or pocket living souvenirs.

life_info.eating: Crustaceans and small fish. Night hunter with a leopard-print tuxedo.
life_info.mating: Pelagic larvae ride currents to new reefs.
life_info.habitat: Coral heads and rocky holes across Caribbean reefs. Usually one eel per favorite hole.

fun_facts: Spots help it vanish against dappled reef light.
Open-mouth look is breathing, not a threat display.
